```{r transformando columnas}
#columnas binarias

data_1$Nmass <- (data_1$`[N]`)*1000 #HELP REVISAR EL ORIGINAL. ORINGIAL NO ESTA EN PORCENTAJE. ENTONCEX HACE FALTA MULTIPLICAR PÖR 100 y luego por 10 para llegar mg por g
data_1$Cmass <- (data_1$`[C_b]`)*1000 #HELP REVISAR EL ORIGINAL. ORINGIAL NO ESTA EN PORCENTAJE. ENTONCEX HACE FALTA MULTIPLICAR PÖR 100 y luego

#por 10 para llegar mg por g

data_1$logNmass <- log(data_1$Nmass) #no el porcentaje
```

#### Funcion tabla
```{r tabla}

tabla <- function(model_list) {

  tab <- modelsummary(
    model_list,
    output = "data.frame",
    statistics = TRUE,
    stars = TRUE,
    gof_map = c("nobs", "r2.marginal", "r2.conditional", "aic")
  )

  # Transponer
  tab_t <- as.data.frame(t(tab))

  # Usar primera fila como nombres
  colnames(tab_t) <- as.character(tab_t[1, ])

  # Hacer nombres únicos 
  colnames(tab_t) <- make.unique(colnames(tab_t))

  # Eliminar fila usada como header
  tab_t <- tab_t[-1, , drop = FALSE]

  # Guardar nombres de modelo
  tab_t$Modelo <- rownames(tab_t)
  rownames(tab_t) <- NULL

  # Reordenar columnas
  tab_t <- tab_t[, c("Modelo", setdiff(names(tab_t), "Modelo")), drop = FALSE]

  # Exportar a Excel
  write.xlsx(tab_t, "model_list_SUB.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE, asTable = TRUE)

  message("✔ Model saved on excel")

  # Retornar tabla para markdown / PDF / HTML
  return(kbl(tab_t, booktabs = TRUE, align = "l"))
}

tabla(models_iWUE_d)
tabla(models_estq_d)
tabla(models_leafstr_d)


```
### Funcion para graficar


```{r}
tabla <- function(lista_modelos) {

  for(nombre in names(lista_modelos)){

    model_list <- lista_modelos[[nombre]]

    tab <- modelsummary(
      model_list,
      output = "data.frame",
      statistics = TRUE,
      stars = TRUE,
      gof_map = c("nobs", "r2.marginal", "r2.conditional", "aic")
    )

    # Transponer
    tab_t <- as.data.frame(t(tab))

    # Usar primera fila como nombres
    colnames(tab_t) <- as.character(tab_t[1, ])
    colnames(tab_t) <- make.unique(colnames(tab_t))

    # Eliminar header
    tab_t <- tab_t[-1, , drop = FALSE]

    # Guardar nombres de modelo
    tab_t$Modelo <- rownames(tab_t)
    rownames(tab_t) <- NULL

    # Reordenar columnas
    tab_t <- tab_t[, c("Modelo", setdiff(names(tab_t), "Modelo")), drop = FALSE]

    # Exportar Excel
    archivo <- paste0("modelos_", nombre, ".xlsx")
    write.xlsx(tab_t, archivo, overwrite = TRUE, asTable = TRUE)

    message(paste("✔ Excel creado:", archivo))
  }

}

listas <- list(
  iWUE = models_iWUE_d,
  est = models_estq_d,
  leafstr = models_leafstr_d)

tabla(listas)
```

```{r GGPLOT }
library(broom.mixed)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

plot_coefs <- function(model, title, control = "C") {

  coefs <- tidy(
    model,
    effects = "fixed",
    conf.int = TRUE,
    conf.level = 0.95
  ) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    mutate(
      term = gsub("^Sub", "", term),
      sig = case_when(
        p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
        p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
        p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
        TRUE            ~ ""
      )
    )

  # 👉 Agregar explícitamente el control
  control_row <- tibble(
    term = control,
    estimate = 0,
    conf.low = 0,
    conf.high = 0,
    sig = ""
  )

  coefs <- bind_rows(control_row, coefs)

  ggplot(coefs, aes(x = term, y = estimate)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, color = "black") +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
      width = 0.15
    ) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = sig, y = conf.high+0.05 * max(abs(coefs$estimate))),
      vjust = -0.6,
      size = 5
    ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
    labs(
      title = title,
      x = "",
      y = "Estimate (± 95% CI)"
    ) +
   scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.2)))+
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
}
```

```{r diagnostiscs common }

plot_diagnostics <- function(model, model_name) {
  
  res <- residuals(model)#residual
  fit <- fitted(model) #model
  
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) #graph
  
  # Residuals vs Fitted
  plot(fit, res,
       xlab = "Fitted values",
       ylab = "Residuals",
       main = paste(model_name, "\nResiduals vs Fitted"))
  abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)
  
  # QQ plot
  qqnorm(res, main = paste(model_name, "\nNormal Q-Q"))
  qqline(res, col = "red", lty = 2)
  
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
  #plot()
  
}
```
